whatItFakes: The wider population's purchases are merged per seller, kind and week of the month and paid monthly instead of after each household's own paydays; count workers always work their full schedule and are paid on the employer's cadence (semimonthly approximated as two monthly dates).
why: Two-level population (owner, Oct 11): only the circle is simulated person by person; the merged flows keep every monthly total equal to the full opening.
replacement: Wider-population spending timed from the counts' pay dates and income, and absence and turnover by industry read from the counts. The rows to check against are sourced (data/research/people/jolts-cps-turnover-absence-2025.json: BLS JOLTS 2025 annual hires, separations, quits and layoffs rates and CPS 2025 absence rates by industry), read by src/core2/turnover-check.ts; the mechanic that uses them is pool item people-residents-cadence-mechanic. Measured Oct 21 (Salem, Utah, seed 07f42052624493fd): hires 2.18 a month against JOLTS 3.3, quits 2.11 against 2.0, layoffs 0.27 against 1.1, separations 2.68 against 3.3.

whatItFakes: A person filled in from the wider population keeps receiving their retirement income through the residents account; their cash share is their opening share of the residents' current cash, and their job's calendar copies the employer's cadence from the fill-in date.
why: Fill-in v2 moves cash, scheduled work and household purchases onto the person's own records; retirement income is tied to per-person award records funded through the outside payer's single obligation.
replacement: Done Oct 12: a filled-in retiree is paid their own award by the same outside payer on the same dates (the pooled retirement flow shrinks by exactly that amount). The cash share is an estimate from opening shares, and the job's calendar follows the employer's cadence, both by design.

whatItFakes: Buyers outside the town are one account per place paying each firm a fixed weekly share of its projected receipts (adjusted with its demand), not individual outside customers, freight orders, Medicaid claims or guests.
why: 11 of 14 closures in the first money year were firms with no customer route at all (owner order M0-money-fix); the share of receipts from outside the town is researched per industry.
replacement: Outside demand from the national and regional economy engines (OPUS-WORLD): exports, government programs and visitors as their own dated buyers.
resolution: Closed as a labeled estimate: the outside buyers' flow is each firm's researched industry share of receipts (src/core2/data/outside-market.json, with value, low and high), and the macro and regional engines already scale it every month (scaleOutsideSales, limitOutsideSales); nothing tops a firm up to its projection.

whatItFakes: Each firm pays cash above twice its industry's median buffer to owners monthly, a fixed tunable share to the town's residents and the rest outside; no firm has recorded owners, retained-earnings policy, taxes or investment.
why: Without payouts, firms kept every dollar of profit and residents ran out of cash within the year (Mill Creek, Oklahoma: firms +$77M, residents $7.7M to $0).
replacement: OPUS-WORLD's business engine: recorded owners (local people or outside), payout and investment decisions from the firm's own conditions, and business taxes. Deleted the core stand-in (the monthly payout flow, its handler and its two parameters). Owners draw from their firm through the business engine: a recorded owner chooses a share of the profit the firm kept from their own money and the firm's cash (business.ts, owner-draw), to local owners as counted or full residents and to outside owners through the recorded outside exchanges.

whatItFakes: Counted residents the opening couldn't place in a town firm (the employment target from ACS/CPS less recorded jobs) earn the place's ACS median earnings (the town's median recorded wage where the place's sample is too thin), paid every two weeks from outside, without employers, commutes or industries.
why: The opening's town workplaces cover only part of the county's industry mix (e.g. 34% in Mill Creek, Oklahoma), so most working residents had no income and the residents' account ran dry within months.
replacement: Recorded jobs for every employed resident: town firms in the missing industries (health care, education, government) and commutes to employers in other places (LEHD LODES origin-destination flows), with their own pay.
resolution: Closed as a labeled estimate: counted workers the opening could not place earn the place's ACS median earnings, a modeled population's out-of-town pay with its ESTIMATED source and spread on the flow, not a faked mechanic.

whatItFakes: A business closed by its owner's choice pays its workers what they've earned (counted workers at once, full workers on their next payday from cash held back), its supplier bills already owed, then settles each open credit line from the cash left (the rest is written off, as in any closure); no assets are sold, so a firm's equipment and property add nothing to what lenders and the owner receive.
why: WORLD's owners needed a way to close a solvent business; a full wind-down (final pay, settling payables, selling assets) is not built yet.
replacement: The closure sells the business's assets (WORLD's business engine records them) before settling lenders and the owner's distribution.

whatItFakes: The part of each household's assigned living cost (CEX basket plus HUD Fair Market Rent) that is not bought from a recorded local seller and is not carried by a bound contract (rent to a landlord, mortgage to the bank, which the housing engine pays) is paid to one outside account on the 1st: no utility or outside store.
why: Rent and non-local spending were never paid, so household cash grew without limit.
replacement: The outside-spending model (category location-quotient leakage) that pays the non-local basket to outside sellers by category. Rent and mortgages are already paid to recorded landlords and the bank by OPUS-WORLD's housing engine (checked Oct 16, Rush Valley, Utah, seed rent1); turn the rest off with collapseToTwoLevels(input, { outsideLivingCosts: false }) once the model exists.
resolution: Closed as a labeled estimate: the counted wider population is a modeled population, so the part of its living cost not bought from a recorded local seller is a CEX and HUD estimate with its source on the flow, and rent and mortgages are already paid to recorded landlords and the bank by the housing engine.

whatItFakes: A named person filled in from a recorded identity (e.g. a state or federal official) gets neutral traits, no family or acquaintances, no cash and a monthly cadence.
why: Traits, kin and past come from the opening's generation world, which a running core doesn't have; GOV needs full officials now (SG-GOV-official-identity-only).
replacement: PEOPLE's trait, kin and past builders seeded from the world seed and the identity (as fill-in of counted residents does), and the official's pay from the public payroll. Done Oct 12 (OPUS-CORE): fillInIdentity gives traits from PEOPLE's openingTemperaments, seeded by the world and the person.

whatItFakes: Counted adults in the town vote as one group per age band: eligible voters are the count times the place's ACS 2020–2024 citizen share of adults blended with the state's CPS 2024 share for the band, turnout is the state's CPS 2024 citizen turnout (national rows where no state row exists, as for the island areas), and every group starts with its county's 2024 presidential two-party margin as its lean (the state's in Alaska, which reports by house district).
why: In a two-level town only about 60 named people vote individually; elections need the counted population to vote from its own records (PLAY's report on GOV's elections). Resolved by the one-electorate change (owner, Oct 14, 2026): the groups are deleted; every counted adult votes from their own record and place in the town's lean order (src/core2/electorate.ts), counted votes are scaled by the place's ACS citizen share (src/core2/electorate-places.ts citizenShareOf), and CPS 2024 turnout is a check in src/core2/electorate.test.ts, not an input.
replacement: Residents' own views (PEOPLE's views engine) set each group's lean, refined by GOV's elections; each counted person's own citizenship once the counts record it.

whatItFakes: At the opening (before any law can change), Social Security's earliest claim age, full retirement age by birth year and the age-70 end of delayed credits are read from a core data table of the same statute GOV's law rows hold. During play, claims are dated from the law in force (GOV's socialSecurityAges) wherever the laws engine runs; a claim already dated keeps its date if Congress changes the ages later.
why: The retirement claim became a decision within the law's bounds before GOV's laws module carries Social Security ages.
replacement: GOV's Social Security ages as law in force (lawInForce), read at the claim date. Done Oct 15 (claude/ss-ages-law-in-force): retirementClaimAgeMonths takes the ages from the law (socialSecurityAges, the law in force at the claim date, or the day-one law for the opening's history); the core table src/core2/data/social-security-ages.json is deleted.

whatItFakes: People who reach their claim age during play, full or counted, start a Social Security award sized like the opening's (a participant-average amount scaled by modeled covered months), paid monthly by the place's outside payer: to the person, or into their place's residents income while they're counted (it follows them when they're filled in). No application, earnings test, spouse or survivor benefit.
why: WORLD's jobs engine retires people during play, and nothing started their benefits, so retirees lost all income.
replacement: GOV's Social Security program: claims read the law in force and awards follow each person's recorded earnings.

whatItFakes: A town whose opening has no recorded teacher job to copy (no private school) gets no public school district.
why: The district's jobs copy a recorded teacher's job, timetable and pay; the old generator has no public school organization to staff. Resolved Oct 13 (OPUS-CORE): a town with no recorded teacher job gets teachers at the OEWS national median teacher pay on a school-day timetable.
replacement: The opening's jobs builder makes teacher jobs from the occupation's OEWS pay and a school-day timetable without a template.

whatItFakes: The villages of Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands come from the game's existing recorded list (carried over from the old place module), not from Census identities.
why: The Census Gazetteer corpus covers the states, D.C. and Puerto Rico only; the island areas need their own identities.
replacement: Census 2020 Island Areas place identities (the research request territory-place-identities), read into the same listing. Oct 14 (OPUS-CORE): the candidate list is built (src/core2/data/places/territory-places-census.json, 158 inhabited villages with Census GEOIDs and 2020 populations, every current key kept, by tooling/build-territory-places.ts); the swap waits until PEOPLE's population builder reads places through the core lookup.

whatItFakes: The town's families with school-age children are ranked by cash per child and the best-off enroll all their children in the private school until the town's state's private share of students (NCES, fall 2021) is reached, each paying the average private tuition. The family's beliefs, the schools nearby and the child's own needs do not yet enter, and enrollment is fixed at the opening.
why: Private schools had no customers at all, so they closed in every town.
replacement: PEOPLE's schools engine: each child's enrollment chosen from the family's income, beliefs and the schools nearby, moving as they change. Means-ranked enrollment replaced the even spread of the town's average on Oct 19.

whatItFakes: The wider population's deaths and births come from rates applied to the counts each month: SSA cohort life tables scaled by the state's 2017 age-adjusted death rate against the nation's (NCHS), and NCHS 2024 national birth rates by mother's age. Whoever has the highest rate is the one who dies or gives birth; nobody's health or family plans decide it.
why: The counted population never changed (owner, Oct 12: the counted rest drifts too).
replacement: Deleted Oct 17 (claude/counted-drift-delete): the counted births and deaths are the renewal engine's counted flows (src/core2/births-counted.ts: NCHS state birth rates by mother's age, life-table chances with the state's death-rate ratio, deaths following serious illnesses), registered under SG-PW8-counted-arrivals; the old drift module ran only in life cores without the renewal engine and stood down in every played world.

whatItFakes: Newcomers to the wider population arrive only into homes a counted household just left, as a household of the same ages and genders with the home's cash, given names people born their year were called (SSA) and a family name drawn from the town's recorded names, and no retirement income or job (the jobs engine may hire them). The town's own state rates apply to every counted household, including relatives' households elsewhere. Leavers' cash stays in town.
why: The counted population should move in and out (owner, Oct 12, ruling 4), and no housing market places counted newcomers yet.
replacement: Deleted Oct 17 (claude/counted-drift-delete): counted people move between places from causes in the counted-moves engine (src/core2/modules/counted-moves.ts), and newcomers are generated by the renewal engine's counted flows (SG-PW8-counted-arrivals); the drift module's own newcomer rule is gone.

whatItFakes: A counted worker whose job a public supplier agreement names as its qualified worker never dies or moves away in the counts.
why: A public supplier agreement's qualification must resolve its named job each month, and nothing yet lets an agreement replace a worker who left.
replacement: When a named worker leaves, the agreement names another qualified worker at the supplier or ends (the finance engine's public supplier rules). Done Oct 14 (OPUS-CORE): supplier agreements now follow whoever does the work and end when nobody does (5ea270be on main), so named counted workers die and move like anyone else.

whatItFakes: Every school-age full person attends the town's public school district (or, in a world opened without it, their town's schools as a place) on the weekdays of one national school calendar (Sept. 1 to June 10, cut at the state's required instructional days where it sets them in days (Education Commission of the States, 2018), the federal holidays by their dates each year, and fixed winter and spring breaks), for the national average school day. Attending is their own choice through the chooser against a full compulsory pull, so in practice every child goes every day: no illness, truancy or family circumstance keeps one home. No grade, class, teacher, homework, private school or homeschooling.
why: School-age people never went to school (M0-13).
replacement: PEOPLE's schools engine: each child's enrolled school (opening-schools), its district calendar and hours, classes with classmates and teachers, and attendance that state law and family circumstances shape.

whatItFakes: Disasters happen only where and when FEMA declared one for the town's county or state (since 2000), as a public news event on the incident's start date. Federal Public Assistance obligated to the county's own government and the town's government (disasters declared since 2020) is paid in full on the declaration date from the U.S. Treasury outside account the game already keeps for Social Security. FEMA housing assistance approved for the town's households (Individuals and Households Program, owners and renters, disasters since 2020) is paid to the town's counted residents on the declaration date, scaled by the world's people over the Census estimate (a town without an estimate takes the whole amount); no single household is chosen, and 36% of household rows don't match a county or town by name. A government kept outside the world receives nothing. The town's households also pay, on the declaration date, for repairing the damage FEMA inspected in owners' homes (scaled the same way), to the town's open builders by their staff or to builders outside the town; the news event carries how many homes FEMA found damaged. Damage to rented homes falls on no landlord, and repairs are paid at once from what households have rather than over months or by insurance. No damage to businesses, public buildings or people; no other applicants (schools, utilities, nonprofits; 13% of assistance rows don't match a county); no new disasters after the records end.
why: The core owns disasters and hazards (BOARD); under no-dice a rate can't decide when one strikes, and the owner hasn't ruled on what should cause new ones.
replacement: The owner's ruling on what causes a disaster in play; damage to businesses, public buildings and people (from NOAA storm episodes), and household aid and repairs reaching the named households that lost homes, with insurance and repairs over time; assistance paid over its real obligation dates to every applicant; a federal FEMA account of its own.

whatItFakes: A cause group spends its money only on ad time, bought through the campaigns engine's ad purchase; it holds no events, sends no mailers and pays none of a cause's own costs.
why: Stress audit defect 2 (Oct 14): groups took donations and never spent them. The ad purchase was the one existing way to buy reach.
replacement: A group chooses among the reach it can buy (events, mailers, press) and a cause's costs (a lawyer, a petition drive where the golden path needs one), read from its members' plans.

whatItFakes: No appointer ever names the player to a town post; the player holds a post only by appointing others as the executive or by winning a seat.
why: Trace audit (Oct 14), item 3: in Tillamook, Oregon (seed 19a393194ce9) the player was appointed public works director with no choice of theirs. The player's decisions are always theirs. Whether an appointer may offer the player a post, for the player to accept or decline, is the owner's call.
replacement: The owner's ruling: either the player is never appointed, or an appointer's choice of the player becomes an offer the player accepts or declines in the conversation, and only an accepted offer fills the post. docs/coordination/OWNER-DECISIONS.md, 'The player's choices are the player's' (Oct 14, night): 'No engine accepts a job, a home, a filing or any choice for the controlled person; the engine offers, the player decides.' Appointers never fill a post with the player on their own; an offer is the player's to accept.

whatItFakes: An estate pays no estate or inheritance tax: no tax series exists for it in the law catalog yet.
why: Owner, Oct 14: the estate pays its debts, then the taxes in force, then the heirs. GOV adds the federal estate tax and the states' estate and inheritance taxes as law series. Resolved by OPUS-GOV (2026-10-14, gov/estate-tax): the series exist and probate reads them (src/core2/laws-death-taxes.ts).
replacement: Probate reads the estate and inheritance tax series in force for the decedent's state and the nation, pays the named treasuries, and the heirs take the rest.

whatItFakes: Nobody holds anything in a trust: every estate passes through probate.
why: Owner, Oct 14: trusts are the simplest real version (assets that pass outside probate), behind an owner decision on how far trusts go in 1.0. Resolved Oct 16, 2026 (core-trusts-background): a person's wealth sets their lean toward a revocable living trust (trustWealthMidpointMinor, trustWealthWeight), and what sits in the trust passes to its beneficiaries outside probate; estate and inheritance taxes still read it.
replacement: The owner's ruling on trusts: at least a revocable living trust a person can make, whose assets pass to its named beneficiaries at death without probate.

whatItFakes: Counted adults who give to a cause group give the mean of what the group's full members' own gift rule gives, once a month, because a counted giver has no drive or cash of their own.
why: CTO, Oct 14: groups raise from the counted population as well as from full people, by the same rule times the count.
replacement: Counted groups carry their own concern by topic and their cash above the buffer, so the same gift rule reads them directly, at the frequency full givers give.

whatItFakes: candidacy.ts (incumbent tie) and legislature.ts (two member ties) still read a relationship's stored level, the closeness at the last contact, instead of today's faded closeness (closenessBetween).
why: Stress audit defect 21 (Oct 14). Every other engine now reads closenessBetween; those two files belong to gov/wiring-votes-and-views this round and OPUS-CORE may not edit them.
replacement: Those three reads call closenessBetween(api.state, a, b) from src/core2/closeness.ts; then this row resolves.

whatItFakes: A law the research records only as in force at the opening (a state's policy answers, a law carried back to the start date) is given an enactment date between one and twenty years before day one, fixed by the world's seed.
why: The starting-law research reads which law is in force on its calibration date, not when each was passed.
replacement: Enactment years from the research for each policy answer, read by the law history (src/core2/past-laws.ts) in place of the seeded age; builder item core-past-law-enactment-years. Started Oct 23, 2026 in data/research/core/state-law-adoption-dates-2025.json for two policies, Medicaid expansion and right-to-work, all 56 places (Wikipedia summaries of the KFF tracker and the National Right to Work Committee timeline, whose own pages refused or showed the dates as images): their 67 laws in force at day one were passed 1.14 to 81.05 years before it, median 11.05. pastUndatedLawAgeYearsLow and High stay ESTIMATED (1 and 20) with those spreads (checked by scripts/research/core-parameters-check.ts).

whatItFakes: The prior election's challenger, a law's sponsor or signer who left office before day one, and the predecessors who held a seat are names drawn from the seed, not people of the world.
why: Only officeholders and the player's circle are full people (two-level population); the people who lost or left are not filled in yet.
replacement: The core's fill-in makes a challenger or former official a full person the moment the player meets or looks them up, matching the name, party and record already written (OPUS-CORE fill-in).

whatItFakes: Archive stories use kinds prefixed 'archive:' in the news engine's story shape, and keep their facts on the story with a pointer in the reader's knowledge.
why: The press session has not yet named a news-archive record kind; asked on PR #4190. Resolved (gov-past-archive-press-writer, 2026-10-16): the press engine names `press.archived` (ARCHIVE_STORY_KIND in src/core2/press-desk.ts) and writes each archive story with `writeArchiveStory` in src/core2/modules/press.ts, from the same wire rule as a live public record; past-news.ts writes no kinds of its own.
replacement: The press engine's own archive kind, written through its writer, once it lands.

whatItFakes: The news archive carries elections, laws, votes, budgets and the deaths of residents' parents, but no business closures from the year before day one. A counted resident's parent who died is not reported either.
why: Resolved (gov-past-closures-archive): the closures are built in src/core2/past-business.ts and archived by past-news.ts; the counted residents' parents' deaths remain, registered as SG-CORE-past-counted-parents-deaths. The generated past holds no closure records dated before the opening: businesses start on day one. Parents' deaths come from the kin generator, which keeps them as facts on full residents only.
replacement: Closures of the town's businesses in the year before day one, generated as records by the business engine, and the counted residents' parents' deaths archived at counted level.

whatItFakes: A counted resident's parent who died in the year before day one is not reported in the news archive.
why: Parents' deaths come from the kin generator, which keeps them as facts on full residents only.
replacement: The counted residents' parents' deaths archived at counted level.

whatItFakes: A territory's prior elections (its delegate and governor) count only the town's own ballots, since territories cast no presidential vote to scale from.
why: The 2024 election research holds presidential totals for the states and D.C. only; territory election returns are not in the repository.
replacement: Each territory's certified 2024 delegate and governor returns (territorial election offices) as research data, read in place of the town's ballots.

whatItFakes: A full person's estate is their cash, the standing payments they owed, and the home of a household whose last member they were (sold when probate closes). Loans, businesses and accounts other than their main one are not settled. A relative who is still only a counted record does not inherit.
why: Money stress audit defect 6 (Oct 14): a dead person's cash stayed on their record. Cash first; the rest of an estate needs property and debt records the core doesn't settle yet.
replacement: Probate that settles debts first, passes businesses by title, and reads a will where the person made one.

whatItFakes: The federal government and other states pay their officials, and receive heirless estates, as outside governments, since only the town's own governments keep treasuries and the town's federal treasury holds only the town's own taxes. Offices the salary table lacks (an auditor, a public service commissioner) are paid the state treasurer's salary; the salary figures are recalled published values marked as estimates in the research file.
why: Money stress audit defect 9 (Oct 14): every official outside the town opened with $0 and no job. The payroll engine pays by attended minute, and scheduling shifts for 1,500 officials would break the speed guard. Resolved Oct 16 (gov-official-salary-through-payroll): each monthly salary is a gross paycheck from the town's state treasury with the law's withholding taken out to each government that keeps a treasury, the pay is counted as spending on the treasury's administration line, and each figure carries its provenance (governors SOURCED for 2023; the rest ESTIMATED with a spread). The federal government and other states still pay their officials as outside parties (SG-CORE-outside-governments).
replacement: A salaried pay basis in the payroll engine so officials are paid by paycheck with withholding; every state's treasury where its officials act; sourced salary rows for every elected office.

whatItFakes: Engines that still read counted people one by one (jobs, business, campaigns, retirement claims, housing, place prices, candidacy) get a person or household record built on demand from the counted group's packed columns, with no past, no ties outside the household and no sources of their own.
why: One model, two tiers (owner, Oct 14): counted people are held once per group; the engines that read them one by one belong to other lanes and move to group reads one at a time.
replacement: Each engine reads counted groups and their counts (reachOf, group fields) instead of one counted person at a time; the views are then deleted.

whatItFakes: A town's districts are the state House districts its population splits into (from the place-district join), else the whole town; city council wards are not modeled.
why: The game has no ward geography; the owner has not said whether council wards should be districts.
replacement: The owner's ruling on what a town's districts are; wards as districts if he wants them. Answered by the owner's Oct 15 ruling and built in gov-council-election-method: each place's council is elected the way its own records say (councilElectionMethod in src/core2/gov-rules/council-election-method.ts: ward seats from a compiled charter, else estimated at large from the ICMA 2018 national shares, basis and citation kept on the office), and offices-local.ts seats the ward seats by part of town. The residents engine's split of a town into state House districts is a different thing (placement of counted voters for state legislative contests, SG-CORE-district-placement) and is not a council shape.

whatItFakes: A counted person built at fill-in has their household, job and coworkers but no relatives living outside their household.
why: Counted people keep no ties outside their household (one model, two tiers); building relatives at fill-in needs the relative generator to run for one person. The owner has not ruled whether that is needed for early access.
replacement: The owner's ruling; if wanted, the opening's relative generator run for one filled-in household, seeded by the world. Built: fillInPerson (src/core2/state.ts) rebuilds the filled-in household's past with buildDeepPast (family histories, src/core2/past-family.ts) and ties to relatives living elsewhere become husks (core.husks), met and filled in later; the opening keeps outside relatives as light husk-tier records (src/core2/data/opening-kin.json). The world-has-a-past work merged Oct 11 to 14.

whatItFakes: A full person out of the player's life for 180 days returns to their counted group (TUNABLE).
why: The owner asked for demotion after 'a long while' without naming how long.
replacement: The owner's number of days. Owner ruling, Oct 15, 2026: 'The days without contact before a met person drifts back into the counted population is a per-world range of 180 to 240 days, drawn once per world at generation (seeded generation is allowed), never a single fixed number.' Built in counted-demotion.ts (demotionDays) from the countedDemotionDays spread.

whatItFakes: Money an engine pays to or takes from a place's counted residents as a whole (an owner's draw to owners who are counted, a pooled property tax bill, a price change on counted households, money left in the place's residents account) is shared by the place's counted groups by their people, not by the households it belongs to.
why: Those engines (business, housing property tax, place prices, unemployment claims) name a place or a counted person but pay the place's residents account; until each passes the person or household, the groups share it.
replacement: Each engine pays counted money through countedPayment with the counted person or household it belongs to (business owners, property tax by owner household, price changes by household), so the right group pays or is paid.

whatItFakes: A town split between state legislative districts places its counted households into the districts by income order, filling each district in proportion to its Census population in the town, so each district holds a slice of the town's income ladder.
why: The game reads only each district's population in the town (Census place-district populations); it has no district-level income, housing or vote tables, and no home locations.
replacement: Each district's own Census tables (ACS by state legislative district: income, tenure, age) and its election results, so households are placed by the district's real mix.

whatItFakes: A filled-in household keeps its share of the place's unplaced workers' pay (counted workers no employer's books hold) as its own flow, untaxed, until it returns to the counts.
why: The opening places only some counted workers in recorded jobs; the rest are paid from one place-level flow with no employer to file a W-2.
replacement: Resolved: a filled-in worker with an unplaced income holds a job (job:commuter:<personId>:<start>) at the place's outside account, paid through the payroll calendar with withholding; demotion ends it and returns the pay to the unplaced pool. Shown in unplaced-fill-in-job.test.ts (pool item core-commuter-job-fill-in).

whatItFakes: A town larger than the opening target (10,000 people, owner decision Oct 9) opens with 10,000 people, not its Census population, so its counts, a law's reach and its money cover only those 10,000. A town smaller than the target opens at its real Census size.
why: The owner set the 10,000 target on Oct 9 before the counted tier was one record per group; whether a bigger town should count its full Census population (each counted household standing for several) is his call.
replacement: The owner's ruling: either keep the cap, or let each counted group of a bigger town carry its Census count with the money and reach scaled to it. docs/coordination/OWNER-DECISIONS.md, 'Town size (day-one audit)': 'a town opens at its real Census size; nothing pads it to 10,000. Follows one model, two tiers (counts must match the place).' Open for the engineers: population.ts still caps a town above the target; it follows the ruling next.

whatItFakes: A known counted relative can receive a death notice, but opening full-to-counted family ties lack recorded closeness; grief is supported only where a relationship record already exists. No closeness is invented by the notifier.
why: The core opening skips relationship initialization when the other person is a husk. The bench also retains the full family closure; the drawn Garden City year had zero known counted deaths, so the notification path has no played-year acceptance yet.
replacement: Resolved Oct 23: the core opening records each full person's tie to a counted relative with openingClosenessHours (state.ts), the bench builds its relatives as counted records through the same opening, births-counted.test.ts fails on a tie without closeness, and births-counted-death-notice.test.ts follows a counted relative's death in a played year to the notice and the full relative's grief.

whatItFakes: The federal government pays its officials (the president, vice president, senators and representatives), and another state's government pays its own, as an outside party recorded on the journal, and receives what escheats to it; their pay is paid in full while the taxes withheld from it go to every treasury the world keeps.
why: The town's federal treasury holds only the town's share of federal taxes (a few hundred thousand dollars a month), too little to pay a national payroll, and no other state keeps a treasury here. Paid from the federal treasury, the president's pay came out at about $500 in a month.
replacement: A federal treasury at national scale and a coarse treasury for every other state, so their officials are paid from them and their estates settle to them.

whatItFakes: Which household is victimized is ranked by income, tenure and household kind (burglary) and by each member's age and income (violent crime), each read from a separate BJS table and multiplied as if independent. Property crime other than burglary uses the burglary ranking because BJS publishes no income or tenure cut for it in the tables used. The ranking overstates the gap between poor renters and rich owners; the place's expected count does not depend on it.
why: Only marginal tables are published in the reports read (BJS cv24, vdhb).
replacement: A joint rate by income, tenure and household kind from the NCVS public-use file or the NCVS Victimization Analysis Tool, and a property-crime cut of its own for theft and motor vehicle theft.

whatItFakes: Crimes happen to households with no offender: nobody decides to offend, so a victimization has no perpetrator, motive or relationship to the victim.
why: A full crime engine (offenders deciding to offend, police, courts) comes later; the web needs only victimization records.
replacement: An offending engine where people decide to offend from their own traits, money and circumstances, so the national rate is a check on its total.

whatItFakes: Arrests follow the crimes this engine records and the police were told of (public safety reads its month record), at each offense's FBI clearance rate and the police the town's lines fund, as counted cases the justice engine files; no officer decides an arrest, so a reported crime is cleared as a share of the month, not one by one.
why: FBI clearance rates by offense type (UCR) apply only to crimes known to police and would need police and court engines to say who is arrested and charged; applying a rate alone would only be a number.
replacement: Police behavior that clears reported crimes one by one from the records (an officer, a lead, the victim's report), with the FBI clearance rates as the check on their totals.

whatItFakes: Vandalism is not a victimization record: the NCVS has no national vandalism rate, so no household is victimized by it, and the web's crime.vandalism index (unemployment-to-vandalism, crime-level-to-vandalism) moves in the ledger only.
why: BJS does not publish a vandalism rate in Criminal Victimization 2024; the web keeps vandalism as an index on the place's own start.
replacement: A sourced national rate for vandalism or criminal mischief (the NCVS household supplement or NIBRS destruction of property), then a record type like the others.
resolution: The FBI's NIBRS estimates give a national rate (Data Year 2024, Indicator Table 1b: 1,859,195 destruction, damage and vandalism incidents, 546.67 per 100,000 persons, 1,076,264 at a residence or hotel), so src/core2/data/crime/victimization.json has a vandalism type (8.04 per 1,000 households, ESTIMATED from the NIBRS count over the households BJS Criminal Victimization 2024 table 2 implies) and the crime engine victimizes households by it in its existing loop, times the web's factor for crime.vandalism (unemployment-to-vandalism, crime-level-to-vandalism); proved by src/core2/law-wiring-crime-web.test.ts. What stays faked: the rate counts only incidents known to police, and no arrest follows a vandalism record (SG-CORE-crime-arrests).

whatItFakes: A firearm homicide is a death, so the victimization records do not make it: crime.firearm-homicide (stand-your-ground-to-homicide, concealed-carry-permit-to-firearm-homicide) stays in the web's ledger and no death follows from it.
why: The NCVS excludes homicide, and a death belongs to the death engine's own causes.
replacement: The death engine reading the web's factor for firearm homicide on each person's cause-specific mortality.
resolution: The death engine's firearm-homicide cause reads the web's factor for crime.firearm-homicide at every age (death-causes.json `reads`, src/core2/death-cause.ts causeMix), so both links move the cause's share of deaths and the death hazard of full and counted people alike; proved by src/core2/death-cause-firearm-homicide.test.ts.

whatItFakes: Each August the town's full families are re-ranked by cash per child and their private school tuition contracts start or end to match the NCES share; the counted families keep the enrollment they opened with.
why: A counted family's tuition is a share of a merged purchase flow with a contract part per household (opening-private-tuition.ts, residents.ts); starting or ending a part at runtime needs a residents-engine move that fill-in also takes back contract by contract.
replacement: Resolved: counted families are ranked with the full families each August (private-tuition-reenroll.ts) and their tuition is a part of the school's merged purchase flow, started or ended with setCountedTuition (modules/residents.ts). Shown in private-tuition-counted.test.ts (pool item core-private-tuition-counted).
